stem: Gauss's law states the electric flux through a closed surface is

rationales.A: closed-surface flux depends on enclosed charge
rationales.B: This mistakes ε₀ for a multiplier on the enclosed charge rather than the divisor Gauss's law requires.
rationales.C: This confuses charge outside the surface with enclosed charge, which contributes zero net flux.
rationales.D: This overgeneralizes the special zero-net-enclosed-charge case (or the magnetic-flux identity) into a universal rule.

stem: Energy stored in a capacitor is

rationales.A: This drops the factor of one-half that comes from integrating V dq up to charge Q.
rationales.B: integrating V dq gives one-half CV²
rationales.C: This divides by V² instead of multiplying, inverting the voltage dependence.
rationales.D: This misplaces the factor of 2 as a coefficient of C divided by V rather than one-half CV².

stem: In electrostatic equilibrium, within the conducting material of a conductor, E is

rationales.A: This reverses the actual physics, assuming free charge concentrates the field rather than canceling it in equilibrium.
rationales.B: Free charges rearrange until the field within the conducting material vanishes.
rationales.C: This mistakes electrostatic equilibrium for merely uniform field conditions; equilibrium in a conductor specifically requires E to vanish everywhere within the conducting material, not merely be constant.
rationales.D: This assumes electrostatic equilibrium implies an oscillating field rather than a static zero field.

stem: Two point charges remain fixed while their separation triples. The force magnitude becomes

rationales.A: This applies direct rather than inverse distance scaling.
rationales.B: This uses inverse-linear scaling and misses the square.
rationales.C: Coulomb force varies as 1/r², so tripling r divides force by nine.
rationales.D: This incorrectly uses an inverse-cube relation.

stem: The electric field due to an isolated negative point charge points

choices.label: D
choices.text: its direction depends on the sign of the test charge

rationales.A: This is the direction for a positive source charge.
rationales.B: The field points in the force direction on a positive test charge, toward a negative source.
rationales.C: This confuses electric point-charge geometry with magnetic field around a current.
rationales.D: Electric-field direction is a property of the source charge and does not depend on the sign of a test charge.

stem: For a line charge λ(s), the differential charge element is

rationales.A: Linear density times differential length gives dq=λ ds.
rationales.B: This uses an area element appropriate to surface charge density.
rationales.C: This uses a volume element appropriate to volume charge density.
rationales.D: The linear charge density already gives charge per unit length, so dq = λ(s)ds; differentiating λ is not required.

stem: Uniform E crosses flat area A whose normal makes angle θ with E. Electric flux is

rationales.A: This uses the angle with the surface rather than the stated angle with its normal.
rationales.B: Flux is the dot product EA cosθ using the surface normal.
rationales.C: This divides by the projection factor instead of multiplying.
rationales.D: This ignores the angle between the electric field and the surface normal; only the normal component contributes to flux.

stem: Charges outside a closed Gaussian surface contribute to

choices.label: B
choices.text: local field but zero net flux contribution

choices.label: D
choices.text: nonzero net flux but no enclosed charge

rationales.A: This incorrectly counts external charge as enclosed.
rationales.B: External charges can affect E locally, but their field lines enter and leave with zero net closed-surface flux.
rationales.C: This ignores the electric field from external sources.
rationales.D: An external charge's field lines enter and leave a closed surface with zero net flux contribution.

stem: Two positive point charges are brought closer together. Their electric potential energy

rationales.A: This reverses the inverse-distance dependence for positive U.
rationales.B: For like charges U=kq₁q₂/r is positive and increases as separation decreases.
rationales.C: This assumes a zero reference means all separations have zero energy.
rationales.D: Negative potential energy applies to opposite-sign charges.

stem: A positive charge is released from rest and acted on only by a static electric field. It tends toward

rationales.A: This sends the charge uphill in potential energy without external work.
rationales.B: For q>0, U=qV, so electric force accelerates it toward lower V and lower U.
rationales.C: For positive charge, higher V means higher, not lower, potential energy.
rationales.D: A potential-energy decrease generally appears as increased kinetic energy.

stem: In electrostatic equilibrium, the electric field just outside a conductor is

rationales.A: This would drive free charges along the surface and violate equilibrium.
rationales.B: Any tangential field would move surface charge, so equilibrium field is normal.
rationales.C: Interior field is zero, but exterior normal field can be nonzero.
rationales.D: Electrostatic equilibrium has no sustained surface current.
